subject: Dinosaurs in Mexico
query: why are people saying dinosaurs in mexico
title: Why are people saying dinosaurs in Mexico? A viral hoax, explained
answer: Blurry clips from Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, of a large winged shape were presented on a Mexican UFO show as a possible surviving pterosaur, a prehistoric flying reptile. Local officials say there is no evidence, and the internet turned the claim into a running joke that Mexico is "under attack by dinosaurs."
body:
When people say there are "dinosaurs in Mexico," they are almost always joking. The phrase riffs on a handful of grainy videos from Ciudad Juárez, the border city across from El Paso, Texas, that show a dark winged silhouette crossing the sky. A typical post pairs a monster-movie clip with a caption like "Mexico is not okay right now," or a friend texts, "Stay inside, the pterodactyls are back."

The story began with a security-camera clip said to come from the Anapra neighborhood of Ciudad Juárez. Local outlet Norte Digital reported on Nov. 9 that it had aired on "No Humano," a program hosted by Jaime Maussan, Mexico's best-known UFO promoter, who suggested the creature resembled a pterosaur. A second clip, reportedly filmed near the city's airport, followed around Nov. 10. Mexican paper La Razón reported that an AI-enhanced image of the supposed creature was also shown. The original camera files have not been made public, so the dates, locations and any editing cannot be verified.

There is no scientific support for the claim. Pterosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, and despite the nickname they were flying reptiles, not dinosaurs. The head of Ciudad Juárez civil protection called the material entertainment with no factual basis, according to Radio Net, and fact-checkers note that a large bird, a distorted camera image or digital editing would explain far more than a living prehistoric animal. By mid-November, a wave of TikTok edits, many of them obviously fake, had turned the sighting into a meme, and Google searches asking why people are talking about dinosaurs in Mexico began climbing.

The trend is only days old, so the jokes may change. For parents and teachers, it is a useful, low-stakes example of how a blurry clip plus a confident claim can go viral before anyone checks it. If a child is worried, the simple answer is that no pterodactyl is flying over Mexico.
in_the_news: Clips of a so-called pterodactyl over Ciudad Juárez spread online in the second week of November 2026, followed by a flood of joke videos.

faq.q: Is there really a pterodactyl in Mexico?
faq.a: No. Pterosaurs went extinct about 66 million years ago, and local officials in Ciudad Juárez say the viral clips show no evidence of one.

faq.q: Where did the Mexico dinosaur videos come from?
faq.a: Blurry clips from Ciudad Juárez that aired in early November 2026 on "No Humano," a Mexican program hosted by UFO promoter Jaime Maussan.

faq.q: What was actually in the videos?
faq.a: It has not been identified. A large bird, camera distortion or digital editing are the likeliest explanations, and the original files have not been released.
